title: Protect Your Pay When Illness Stops Work
meta_description: Build a UK income-protection plan around sick pay, essential bills, waiting periods, policy definitions, honest underwriting and a practical claim kit.

sections.heading: Insure the Paycheque That Funds Everything
paragraphs: The opening photograph shows an injured adult at home with a cast and crutches. The interruption is visible before any policy language appears: a body that cannot do its normal work can stop earnings while rent, food, utilities and debt continue. Income protection addresses that cash-flow risk; it is not insurance for a phone, car or appliance.

Begin with the household dependency test. Add the monthly costs that continue if work stops, then identify which depend on one person’s labour. Include housing, council tax, food, utilities, transport, care, minimum debt payments and essential insurance. Separate survival costs from spending that could pause. The result is the income gap to protect, not automatically the whole salary.

Map existing protection before buying anything. Record employer sick pay, Statutory Sick Pay eligibility, savings, partner income, benefits, union support and any policy already attached to work, a mortgage or a professional body. Write amounts, waiting periods, duration, tax treatment and conditions. A vague belief that work “covers sickness” is not evidence.

Model three absences: eight weeks, one year and permanent loss of the current occupation. Short absences test emergency savings and employer pay; long absences expose the end of both. Permanent disability tests whether retraining or a different occupation is realistic. Each horizon can require a different combination of cash, insurance and career contingency.

Define success as maintaining essential decisions, not reproducing every pound of gross pay. Benefits commonly replace only part of earnings and can interact with other income. The target should prevent arrears and rushed asset sales while leaving an incentive and practical path back to work. Use conservative figures and current verified rules.

Protect first against the event the household cannot absorb. Replacing a phone may be annoying; losing years of earnings can reshape housing, retirement and children’s opportunities. Premium affordability matters, but comparing a monthly premium only with gadget cover ignores the scale and duration of the underlying risk.

Set an annual review date and life-event triggers: job change, salary change, self-employment, mortgage, child, divorce, health diagnosis or employer-benefit revision. Income protection is a living household control. A policy chosen once and forgotten can become inadequate, duplicated or impossible to claim under changed circumstances.

sections.heading: Build the Income-Interruption Ledger
paragraphs: Create a one-page ledger with four columns: source, monthly amount, start date and end date. Add salary, contractual sick pay, statutory support, savings withdrawals, partner income and insured benefit. Then build a matching expense timeline. The point is to see when income falls, not merely the annual total.

Verify employer terms from the contract, handbook and HR, not colleague memory. Distinguish full pay, half pay and statutory-only periods. Ask whether service length, probation, previous absence or notification rules alter entitlement. Record who must be contacted, by when and what medical evidence is required. Keep the answer outside the work account.

Review [[S1|current Statutory Sick Pay guidance]] for eligibility, amount and duration, because rules and reforms can change. Do not assume every worker or form of self-employment qualifies. Benefits may provide a floor, but the timing and amount may not match household commitments. Use an official calculator or specialist advice for personal eligibility.

Calculate the monthly gap at each stage. If essential spending is £2,100, employer pay supplies £1,500 and other reliable income supplies £300, the gap is £300 before any contingency. Repeat after employer pay ends. Include additional costs of illness, such as heating, travel, treatment, accessibility or paid care.

Stress-test inflation and delayed payment. A claim may require evidence and assessment; benefits can take time; employer payroll errors occur. Keep a separate liquidity line showing cash available immediately. Insurance that eventually pays does not replace the need for money during the first weeks, especially when a policy has a deferred period.

Avoid counting the same protection twice. A workplace policy and private policy may have coordination limits, while savings pledged to a house deposit cannot simultaneously fund a year of absence without changing the plan. Label assets by purpose and decide explicitly which can be used.

Share the ledger with the other adult who would manage bills during illness. Store policy numbers, contacts, consent and claim steps securely. Income interruption is hardest to administer when the insured person is unwell. A simple, accessible record is part of the protection, not administrative decoration.

sections.heading: Understand What Income Protection Actually Does
paragraphs: Long-term income protection usually pays a regular benefit when illness or injury prevents work under the policy definition, after a chosen waiting period. It differs from critical-illness cover, which pays a lump sum only for specified diagnoses, and life insurance, which responds to death. Accident-only cover is narrower because many long absences arise from illness.

The incapacity definition matters more than the marketing headline. “Own occupation” generally tests whether the claimant can perform their specific occupation; “suited occupation” or “any occupation” can impose a broader work-capacity test. Read the exact contract, including how duties, hours, earnings and partial capacity are assessed.

Check the benefit basis and maximum. Insurers commonly limit replacement to a percentage of pre-disability earnings and may deduct specified other income. Self-employed applicants need clear evidence of earnings under the policy definition. A high selected benefit does not guarantee that amount if verified earnings later support less.

The deferred period is the time between incapacity and insured payments. Align it with employer sick pay and emergency cash. A longer wait can reduce premium, but it is unsafe if cash runs out earlier. Draw the timeline rather than selecting four, eight, thirteen or twenty-six weeks by price alone.

Benefit duration can be short, fixed-term or continue to a stated age while valid incapacity persists. Short cover may handle recovery but leaves catastrophic long-term risk. Compare the saving in premium with the household’s ability to fund the uncovered years. The cheapest quote can remove the protection that motivated the purchase.

Inflation protection affects future purchasing power. A level benefit can erode during a long claim, while an escalating option may cost more and have caps. Also check whether cover and premium are guaranteed, reviewable or age-banded. Ask what can change and what cannot after acceptance.

Read exclusions, waiting rules, residency requirements, medical evidence, claim notification and return-to-work provisions. Do not infer coverage from a product name. The contract, schedule and disclosed information determine the promise. Keep copies of the exact documents issued, not only a comparison-site summary.

sections.heading: Use Employer Cover Without Depending on It Blindly
paragraphs: Workplace sick pay and group income protection can be valuable because underwriting may be simplified and the employer may fund the premium. Obtain the scheme booklet and a personalized benefit statement. Confirm the insured salary definition, replacement percentage, deferred period, maximum term, escalation, deductions and who receives the payment.

Ask what happens when employment ends. Group cover usually belongs to the employer’s scheme, not the employee, and may stop after resignation, redundancy or dismissal. Some plans offer continuation or conversion options under deadlines. A benefit that disappears with the job creates concentration risk precisely when health can also affect employment.

Understand the employer’s role during a claim. Group benefits may be paid to the employer, which then continues payroll subject to scheme and employment terms. The insurer paying the employer does not necessarily guarantee indefinite employment. Read absence, capability and termination policies alongside the insurance booklet.

Check whether bonuses, commission, overtime, dividends and pension contributions count as insured earnings. A headline percentage of basic salary can be much less than normal household income. For variable pay, learn which reference period applies. Design essential spending around the covered figure, not the best recent month.

Coordinate private and group cover. A private insurer may reduce benefit when other income is received, or the aggregate may be capped. Give accurate information at application and claim. Duplication that cannot pay is wasted premium, while a portable private layer can still be useful if employment changes.

Record the evidence process: fit notes, occupational-health assessment, regular reports and rehabilitation contact. Follow employer notification rules promptly. Keep personal copies of relevant correspondence lawfully, but never remove confidential employer or client information. The claim should be documented without breaching workplace obligations.

Review cover before changing jobs, reducing hours or becoming self-employed. Health changes after leaving can make equivalent individual terms expensive or unavailable. Do not cancel existing protection until replacement terms are issued, checked and in force, and never conceal medical facts to obtain them.

sections.heading: Measure the Household Gap, Not the Salary Headline
paragraphs: The midpoint photograph shows a couple using bills, a calculator and a laptop at their kitchen table. This is the correct unit of analysis: a claim exists to keep the household functioning. Start with bank statements and actual annual costs rather than a rounded guess based on take-home salary.

Classify expenses as essential, reducible, pausable and one-off. Essentials include safe housing, food, utilities, care, core transport and minimum contractual payments. Reducible items need a realistic lower level. Pausable spending may have cancellation fees. One-off medical or adaptation costs require a contingency line.

Build a month-by-month cash runway. Employer pay may fall in stages; savings may earn interest; annual insurance, school or maintenance bills arrive unevenly. A monthly average can hide a crisis in month three. Put due dates against expected inflows and preserve a minimum cash floor.

Include the healthy partner’s risk. Their earnings may fall if they provide care, travel to appointments or manage children. Two incomes are not fully independent when one illness changes the other person’s capacity. Test whether outsourcing care is possible and what it costs.

Treat debt strategically. Insurance should not be selected solely to preserve optional overpayments, but arrears on housing or priority commitments can have serious consequences. List creditor hardship contacts and any payment protection separately. Do not assume lenders will automatically pause payments.

Choose a coverage target with a rationale. It may equal the essential gap plus a modest contingency, subject to insurer limits. Keep emergency savings for the deferred period and claim friction. Excessively high cover can waste premium or exceed allowable replacement; too little transfers a predictable shortfall back to the household.

Re-run the budget under partial return to work. Many policies offer proportionate or rehabilitation benefits when earnings remain reduced, but wording varies. Model reduced hours, commuting, treatment and childcare. A staged return can improve health and income without pretending recovery is all-or-nothing.

sections.heading: Choose the Waiting Period Deliberately
paragraphs: The waiting period is a financing decision. Match the first insured payment to the point where employer pay and accessible savings can no longer cover essentials. If full sick pay lasts twelve weeks, a thirteen-week deferred period may align; if employment provides only a statutory floor, the household may need a shorter wait or larger reserve.

Use conservative timing. Payroll and claims do not always arrive on the first expected day, so include a buffer. Confirm whether the deferred period restarts after a relapse and how linked periods of incapacity are treated. Repeated short absences can expose gaps that a long-term policy never reaches.

Price at several waiting periods, but compare identical definitions, duration, escalation and options. A lower quote with a longer wait is not the same protection. Record the monthly saving and the additional cash reserve required; then decide which is cheaper and more resilient for the household.

Keep the deferred-period reserve liquid and low risk. Money intended for next month’s rent should not depend on selling volatile investments. Separate it from the general emergency fund if that improves discipline. Replenish withdrawals after an absence before resuming optional goals.

Self-employed people should include business survival. Personal expenses may pause more slowly than revenue, while software, premises, insurance and key staff costs continue. Personal income protection does not automatically cover business overheads. Map business and household obligations separately and investigate appropriate specialist cover.

Do not shorten the waiting period merely because savings feel uncomfortable to use. Insurance is most valuable for losses the household cannot efficiently retain; cash can handle frequent small interruptions. Conversely, do not lengthen it to achieve an attractive premium when the required reserve does not exist.

Document the chosen bridge: employer pay first, then named savings, then insured benefit. Add claim-notification dates and the person responsible. The bridge should work on a difficult day without improvisation, credit-card dependence or selling long-term assets at an unfavourable time.

sections.heading: Interrogate Definitions, Exclusions and Underwriting
paragraphs: Complete applications accurately and fully. Medical history, occupation, duties, hours, earnings, smoking, travel and dangerous activities can affect terms. Answer the question asked and seek clarification when unsure. A cheaper policy obtained through incomplete disclosure can become the most expensive option if a claim is disputed.

Occupation is more than a job title. Describe physical tasks, travel, machinery, driving, lifting, stress exposure and time split. Two people called directors may have entirely different risk. Keep a copy of the submitted application and corrections so later evidence can be compared with what the insurer assessed.

Underwriting may offer standard terms, premium loading, exclusions, postponed consideration or refusal. Read any exclusion word for word and ask for examples of its scope. A back exclusion can be material for a manual worker; a mental-health exclusion can remove a major cause of long absence. Do not judge only by acceptance.

Compare guaranteed and reviewable premiums. Guaranteed does not necessarily mean every aspect is fixed, so check contractual conditions. Reviewable pricing can change by specified factors. Model affordability at older ages and decide what happens if premium rises. Cover cancelled after health worsens may be difficult to replace.

Check claim tests, evidence frequency and insurer support. Rehabilitation, proportionate benefit, waiver of premium, relapse treatment and career-break rules can materially change value. Ask whether temporary overseas residence, unemployment, parental leave or occupational change affects cover.

Use a regulated adviser where complexity, medical history, variable earnings or multiple policies make comparison difficult. Verify authorization through [[S2|the FCA register]] and understand whether advice is independent, restricted and fee- or commission-funded. A salesperson’s confidence is not a substitute for a suitability record.

Never cancel old cover during underwriting. Wait until new terms, exclusions, premium, start date and cancellation rights have been checked. If the new offer is worse, preserving existing terms may be rational. Health information learned during the process can change future availability.

sections.heading: Fit Cover to Employment Status
paragraphs: Employees should begin with contractual and group benefits. Confirm whether salary continues, whether insurance is discretionary, and how a claim interacts with capability procedures. Job security and insured income are related but separate. Keep a portable plan for the loss of workplace benefits after a move.

Sole traders need evidence of earnings and must distinguish turnover, profit and drawings. The insurer’s earnings definition controls the claim maximum. Maintain timely accounts, tax records and business statements. Artificially low declared profit may reduce tax today but can also reduce provable insured income and borrowing capacity.

Company directors paid through salary and dividends require specialist wording. Some contracts recognize dividends under conditions; others focus on salary. Do not assume the benefit illustration reflects the eventual evidence test. Ask the adviser to record the rationale and documents required.

Contractors should examine gaps between assignments, limited-company structures and occupational changes. Cover may respond to medically defined incapacity, not a contract ending or market downturn. Income protection is not unemployment insurance. Maintain a separate reserve for ordinary commercial gaps.

Workers with several jobs must check whether all occupations and earnings are covered and what happens if they can perform one role but not another. Disclose every material duty. The correct policy structure may differ from a simple percentage of combined income.

People taking parental leave, career breaks or reduced hours should review benefit basis before the change. Some policies preserve cover under specified terms; others recalculate. Notify the insurer when required. Avoid paying for a historic benefit that cannot be supported by current earnings.

For every status, design a career contingency alongside insurance: transferable skills, professional network, accessible training and realistic alternative duties. Insurance replaces some money during incapacity; it does not remove the value of rehabilitation or a sustainable route back to earning.

sections.heading: Prepare for a Claim Before Illness
paragraphs: The late photograph shows insurance paperwork being examined line by line. That is the right behaviour before a claim: understand the contract while healthy and able to organize evidence. Highlight notification deadlines, deferred period, incapacity definition, exclusions, claim contact and consent requirements.

Create a secure claim kit containing policy schedule, wording, application, employer scheme booklet, adviser suitability letter, earnings evidence and contact details. Tell a trusted person where it is. Do not store the only copy on an employer device that becomes inaccessible during prolonged absence.

Maintain normal medical care and accurate occupational records; do not create unnecessary documentation solely for insurance. During illness, seek appropriate treatment and follow reasonable clinical advice. Claim evidence commonly connects diagnosis, functional limits and occupational duties, not diagnosis alone.

Notify the insurer and employer promptly under their procedures even if payment starts later. Ask what forms and financial records are required. Keep a dated communication log and copies of submitted material. Correct factual mistakes calmly and in writing.

Describe function precisely: which duties cannot be performed, for how long, with what restrictions and why adjustments are insufficient. Avoid exaggeration and understatement. A credible claim explains the link between health and the insured work definition using medical and occupational evidence.

Plan for reassessment and return to work. Ask how therapeutic work, reduced hours, rehabilitation and partial earnings affect benefit before starting. Coordinate clinician, employer and insurer where appropriate. An unsupported rushed return can relapse; an unnecessarily delayed return can harm confidence and career.

If a claim is declined, request the reason and policy basis, use the insurer’s complaint process and preserve deadlines. [[S3|the Financial Ombudsman Service]] may review eligible unresolved complaints. Obtain specialist advice where needed; do not assume an initial decision is necessarily final.

sections.heading: Avoid Product Confusion and False Substitutes
paragraphs: Critical-illness insurance pays for listed conditions meeting contractual definitions, usually as a lump sum. It can help with major adjustments or debt, but many disabling conditions will not qualify. It does not automatically replace monthly earnings for every medically supported absence.

Life insurance protects dependants after death, not the insured person’s living costs during illness. Mortgage life cover can clear housing debt on death yet leave no income during years of incapacity. These products can complement income protection; they should not be treated as interchangeable.

Accident, sickness and unemployment policies are often shorter-term and may use different exclusions, benefit limits and renewal structures. Accident-only plans omit illness. Payment-protection cover may serve one debt rather than the whole household budget. Compare the actual trigger, amount and duration.

Emergency savings are essential but finite. Divide accessible savings by the monthly income gap, then reduce the result for contingencies. A £12,000 reserve does not represent twelve months if the gap is £1,500 and medical costs rise. Cash bridges a wait; long-term insurance transfers catastrophic duration.

State benefits provide vital support but eligibility, assessment and amounts are governed by current rules and personal circumstances. Do not build a precise plan from online anecdotes. Use official guidance and accredited benefits support, then retain a margin for timing and reassessment.

Investments and pensions are not frictionless substitutes. Selling during a market fall can crystallize loss, and pension access may be restricted or damage later security. Income protection can preserve long-term assets, but premium must remain affordable. Coordinate protection with saving rather than presenting them as rivals.

Reject policies sold through fear or a single cheap monthly figure. A sound recommendation connects household gap, occupation, wait, duration, definition, exclusions and existing benefits. If the seller cannot explain those links in plain language, pause and obtain another view.

sections.heading: Compare Policies With a Claims-First Scorecard
paragraphs: Create a comparison table before looking at brand or premium. Rows should include incapacity definition, deferred period, benefit amount, duration, escalation, premium basis, exclusions, partial benefit, rehabilitation, career-break rules, claim service and financial strength. Put premium last so it does not erase structural differences.

Score suitability, not generosity in isolation. An own-occupation definition may matter greatly for a specialist; escalation may matter for a young worker with decades of exposure; a short benefit term may be unacceptable where the household cannot self-fund. Apply weights based on the risk ledger.

Request personalized illustrations and specimen wording, then reconcile them. Marketing summaries often omit conditions. Write unresolved questions and obtain answers in a durable form. Where an adviser recommends one contract, the suitability letter should explain why alternatives and exclusions fit the stated needs.

Test four claim stories: musculoskeletal illness, mental-health absence, cancer treatment and an accident that permits some other work. These are not predictions or coverage promises. They force the reader to locate definitions, exclusions, evidence and partial-return rules rather than assuming every incapacity works the same way.

Assess affordability under stress. Premium is another bill that must continue when earnings are uncertain, although waiver provisions may apply after claim acceptance. Model premium increases where reviewable and a temporary income reduction before the deferred period. Avoid over-insuring at a level likely to be cancelled.

Check the insurer and intermediary through official regulatory channels. Read complaint data carefully without treating raw counts as a league table because size differs. Financial strength, claims philosophy and service matter, but no statistic overrides the written contract and individual facts.

Record the final reason in one paragraph: the gap protected, start point, end point, definition and principal compromise. If that sentence cannot be written, the policy may not be understood. Keep rejected quotes only long enough for an audit trail, then dispose of personal data securely.

sections.heading: Run an Annual Protection Drill
paragraphs: Once a year, simulate an absence beginning tomorrow. Can the household find the policies, contact employer and insurer, access the deferred-period reserve and pay the next month’s essentials? A drill exposes inaccessible passwords, stale beneficiaries, missing earnings evidence and assumptions about partner capacity.

Update salary, occupation, duties, hours and employment status. Notify insurers when the contract requires it and request written confirmation of changes. Increased earnings may justify more cover, while reduced earnings can constrain claim maximum. Do not simply raise the direct debit and assume the benefit changed.

Rebuild the expense floor from statements. Housing, childcare, energy, debt and care needs change. Compare the new gap with employer pay, state support assumptions, savings and policy benefit. Adjust only after checking underwriting consequences and replacement risk.

Review medical and lifestyle changes honestly, but do not volunteer information outside contractual duties without advice. Existing guaranteed cover may not re-underwrite routine changes, while an increase or new policy may. Understand the process before replacing valuable terms.

Test provider contact details and claim forms, then update the household claim kit. Confirm a trusted person knows where authority and consent documents are stored. Remove expired copies securely while retaining the issued wording that governs the current contract.

Use life events as off-cycle triggers: marriage, separation, child, mortgage, inheritance, business launch, redundancy, job move or approaching retirement. Protection needs can fall as well as rise. Paying indefinitely for an obsolete gap is not prudent.

End with a decision: retain, amend, replace or intentionally self-insure. Never cancel before replacement is live and checked. The purpose is not to own more insurance; it is to keep essential household choices intact when health interrupts the work that normally pays for them.

sections.heading: Create a Layered Plan You Can Sustain
paragraphs: Use layers in sequence. The first layer is prevention and safe work; the second is accessible cash; the third is employer and statutory support; the fourth is insured income; the fifth is rehabilitation and alternative earning capacity. No layer is perfect, but together they reduce single-point failure.

Set the cash layer to cover the selected deferred period plus claim friction and deductibles. Keep it liquid and clearly named. Continue retirement investing only after the protection bridge is credible; otherwise a short illness can force expensive debt or asset sales that undo long-term progress.

Choose insurance for severity and duration the household cannot retain. A policy with an appropriate definition and long benefit period may deserve priority over multiple narrow add-ons. Keep premium within a budget that survives ordinary income variation. Lapsed cover protects nothing.

Integrate health and workplace practice without implying illness is always preventable. Use safety equipment, reasonable adjustments, leave and clinical support. Maintain skills and networks that enable a different role if capacity changes. Insurance pays money; adaptation rebuilds agency.

Give each adult a role in the plan. One may maintain documents, another track cash and contacts. Discuss privacy, consent and how bills would be prioritized. The conversation should occur while everyone is well, not during a hospital discharge or capability meeting.

Measure the plan through coverage of the essential gap, months of liquidity, clarity of claim steps and portability after a job change. Do not measure it by number of policies. Remove duplication and redirect savings to weak layers.

The final principle is simple: insure the income stream before insuring replaceable objects. A phone can be bought again; years of lost earnings cannot. A disciplined ledger, suitable contract, honest underwriting, accessible reserve and practiced claim process turn that principle into practical household resilience.

summary: Income protection addresses the risk that illness or injury stops earnings while household bills continue. Begin with essential monthly spending, then map employer sick pay, statutory support, savings, partner income and existing insurance by amount, start date and end date. The uncovered amount—not automatically the whole salary—is the protection gap.

Model an eight-week absence, one year and permanent loss of the current occupation. Short absences test cash and employer pay; long absences expose when both end. Include extra costs for treatment, travel, heating, accessibility and care. Keep immediate liquidity because insured or state payments may begin only after evidence and assessment.

Understand the contract. Income protection commonly pays a regular benefit after a deferred period when incapacity meets the policy definition. Check own-occupation versus broader tests, benefit percentage, earnings evidence, deductions, duration, escalation, premium basis, exclusions, partial return-to-work support and claim rules. It differs from critical-illness, life, accident-only and unemployment cover.

Align the waiting period with verified employer pay and an accessible reserve. Compare quotes on identical definitions and duration; a cheaper premium achieved by adding months without income is not equivalent. Employees should inspect group benefits and portability. Sole traders, directors, contractors and multiple-job workers need wording that recognizes their actual duties and provable earnings.

Complete underwriting accurately and keep the submitted application. Describe occupation by duties rather than title. Read every exclusion and do not cancel existing cover until replacement terms are issued, checked and active. Complex medical history, variable income or several policies may justify advice from an appropriately regulated adviser.

Prepare a claim kit before illness: policy schedule and wording, employer booklet, application, earnings evidence, contacts and notification deadlines. Store it securely outside an employer account and tell a trusted person where it is. During a claim, connect medical restrictions to occupational duties, keep a communication log and understand partial-return rules before resuming work.

Compare policies with a claims-first scorecard covering definition, wait, amount, duration, inflation, exclusions, rehabilitation, service and affordability. Put premium last. Test several realistic claim scenarios to locate the relevant wording; never treat examples as promises of coverage.

Run an annual drill and after every major life event. Update salary, duties, household costs, savings and workplace benefits. The strongest plan layers safe work, liquid cash, employer and statutory support, suitable insurance, rehabilitation and portable skills. Its purpose is not to own more policies but to preserve essential household choices when health interrupts earnings.

Workplace cover deserves close inspection rather than automatic trust or rejection. Verify the insured salary, payment route, escalation, deductions and what happens when employment ends. Group insurance can be valuable, but it may belong to the employer and disappear after a job change. Coordinate private and workplace benefits so premiums are not funding a benefit that aggregate limits would prevent.

The household budget must include more than routine direct debits. Illness can increase heating, transport, treatment, childcare and paid-care costs while a partner’s earnings also fall. Build a month-by-month runway because annual averages conceal timing. Keep deferred-period money liquid and separate from investments or a deposit that the household is unwilling to use.

Insurance is only one layer. Safe work, reasonable adjustments, accessible savings, statutory and employer support, rehabilitation and transferable skills all matter. Document who will notify providers, find records and prioritize bills if the insured person cannot. A product becomes useful protection only when the household can sustain its premium, understand its promise and operate the claim process under stress. Review the complete arrangement every year and after changes to work, pay, family, housing or health. Retain suitable existing terms until any replacement has been fully issued and checked.

faq.question: Is income protection the same as critical-illness cover?
faq.answer: No. Income protection generally pays regular income for qualifying incapacity; critical-illness cover pays a lump sum only for specified conditions meeting definitions.

faq.question: How much income should I insure?
faq.answer: Start with the verified essential household gap and insurer benefit limits, then account for existing support and tax treatment.

faq.question: What is a deferred period?
faq.answer: It is the period a qualifying incapacity must continue before insured payments begin. Match it to employer pay and liquid savings.

faq.question: Does workplace cover follow me to a new job?
faq.answer: Often it does not. Check the scheme booklet and any continuation option before leaving.

faq.question: Can self-employed people buy cover?
faq.answer: Often yes, but earnings evidence and policy definitions are crucial. Turnover, profit and drawings are not interchangeable.

faq.question: Will every illness be covered?
faq.answer: No. Coverage depends on the incapacity definition, exclusions, disclosures, evidence and other contractual terms.

faq.question: When should protection be reviewed?
faq.answer: At least annually and after a job, salary, family, mortgage, business or health-related change.

glossary.definition: Insurance designed to pay regular benefits for qualifying incapacity under the contract.
The waiting time before a valid insured benefit begins.
An incapacity test tied to the insured person’s specified occupation.
The maximum period a qualifying claim can be paid.
A stated circumstance or condition the policy does not cover.
Assessment used to decide terms, price and exclusions.
Protection arranged under an employer or organization scheme.
Potential partial payment where reduced capacity also reduces earnings.
A premium that may change under contractual review terms.
Essential financial need remaining after reliable support is deducted.
